precepts.point: And his chambers by wrong. Was stealing all the gold out of Haiti wrong? Was creating coups in every single country in South America wrong?

note.label: Esau the Hater, Liar, and Killer

precepts.why:
Woe, meaning destruction, is on him that builds his house by unrighteousness, and Habakkuk shows what that house is built on: “What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?”

So they practise idolatry. They have statues, and they bow down to them. The Bible says there is no profit in those things. A graven image is a teacher of lies, and the man who makes it trusts in the work of his own hands, a dumb idol that cannot speak.

That is the church of Esau, the hater, liar and killer. I can never understand how somebody in this modern day and age can be a Catholic: the same church that enslaved you, the same church that has statues all over the place. You can clearly read the Bible and say that this is not the way.

The house built by unrighteousness, by slavery and by robbing and pillaging countries, and the church of statues are the same house. The teacher of lies stands in the middle of it, and the woe of Jeremiah is on all of it.

precepts.text: For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him. So he is not the God of the dead. So that church is the church of the dead, because they worship the dead.
precepts.point: And his chambers by wrong. Was stealing all the gold out of Haiti wrong? Was creating coups in every single country in South America wrong?

note.label: Esau the Hater, Liar, and Killer

precepts.why:
Christ says of his Father: “For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.” So the Most High is not the God of the dead.

That church, with its statues all over the place that the people bow down to, is the church of the dead, because they worship the dead. They pray to dead men and graven images, the dumb idols Habakkuk calls a teacher of lies, and the God of Israel is not in that.

It is the same church that enslaved us and built its house by unrighteousness, the house Jeremiah pronounces woe upon: “Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong”. A people who worship the dead cannot be serving the living God, and that is why a so-called Black Catholic should come out of it. The God of the living is the God of the ones who keep his word, not the God of the statues.

precepts.text: Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong; that useth his neighbour's service without wages, and giveth him not for his work.
precepts.point: You see that last sentence: spacious public spaces for worshippers and pilgrims. Meaning the other nations had a place now; they could come and look at what was going on in the temple. That was not in the original design that God gave us. Herod added it. Herod was an Idumean, an Edomite, and this Edomite wanted favor with the Jews.
precepts.why:
The second temple did not look good in comparison to Solomon's, so King Herod the Great, around 20 to 19 BC, began a massive expansion and renovation: to beautify the site, impress the Roman world, and win favor with his Jewish subjects. He doubled the Temple Mount platform with giant retaining walls, used enormous white limestone blocks, some over 500 tons, trimmed the temple with gold, and added grand colonnades, entry gates and spacious public spaces for worshippers and pilgrims. That last part means the other nations now had a place to come and look at what was going on in the temple. That was not in the original design God gave us. Herod added it.

Jeremiah is read against that building: “Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong; that useth his neighbour’s service without wages, and giveth him not for his work”.

Herod was an Idumean, an Edomite, despised by the Judahites because he was not one of their own stock. He hated the people of Judah, executed forty-five of their leaders, and destroyed the priestly line of Hyrcanus. All that building was to get in good graces, and it was built by unrighteousness and by wrong.

precepts.text: Concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: they shall not lament for him.
precepts.point: The same standard fell on Jehoiakim the son of Josiah: they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother, or, Ah lord.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

precepts.why:
The same standard fell on a king. “Therefore thus saith the Lord concerning Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah; They shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother! or, Ah sister! they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah lord! or, Ah his glory!”

Concerning Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, they shall not lament for him. As Aaron and his sons were not to uncover their heads or rend their clothes for Nadab and Abihu, who died in the midst of sin, so no one was to lament for Jehoiakim. Whom the Most High judges in sin is not to be mourned over.
